arxiv-2603-26443: Arends, Peterson, and Weich start a study of resonances on finite-type graphs of groups. The work mirrors spectral theory for finite-type hyperbolic surfaces and manifolds. They look at regular graphs built from groups and study the resolvent of the adjacency operator. They prove the resolvent extends in a meromorphic way and describe the resonant states in geometric terms. Unlike the surface case, these graphs hold only finitely many resonances, and they can be computed in closed form. Examples from curves over finite fields show the same traits.
arxiv-2603-26643: Lin, Liu, Lee, and Jia propose a boundary neuron method for solving partial differential equations. The unknown boundary function is fitted by a shallow network inside a boundary integral form. Hidden parameters are drawn at random and frozen, so the task shrinks to a linear least squares solve. That design keeps the dimension cut of boundary methods and skips nonconvex gradient training. For elliptic problems they prove convergence and error bounds for both boundary and interior values. Tests on Laplace and Helmholtz cases rival the boundary element method.
arxiv-2603-26743: Lee and Har steer sparse autoencoder features to control dynamic head pruning in vision transformers. Pruning redundant attention heads saves compute, but past rules are hard to read or steer. An autoencoder trained on the final layer's residual stream splits dense codes into sparse, legible parts. Amplifying chosen parts shifts which heads get pruned for each class. For the bowl class, accuracy rises from 76% to 82% while head use drops from 0.72 to 0.33, driven by two heads.
arxiv-2603-27243: Lv and co-authors build a microscopic theory of gamma decay from giant resonances in superfluid nuclei. Experiments can now measure gamma rays from giant and pygmy resonances to low-lying states. No microscopic description existed for them. Their Skyrme quasiparticle vibration model treats both states as QRPA phonons. All second-order quasiparticle-phonon diagrams and polarization effects are included. The same Skyrme functional serves the ground state and the interaction vertices. For cerium-140's dipole resonance, predicted widths run 200 to 420 eV. The branching ratio lands between 0.75 and 1.20 percent.
arxiv-2603-27343: Hou and co-authors present WMF-AM, a probe of working memory in large language models. The probe tracks cumulative state across K operations inside one query, with no scratchpad. Depth K is a dial, so difficulty adapts as models improve. The core task is arithmetic accumulation across 28 models from 12 families. Matched non-arithmetic versions use permissions, schedules, and inventories instead. Three ablations show cumulative load itself, not arithmetic skill, drives failure. The diagnostic is lightweight and can be recalibrated over time. Code and data are publicly released.
arxiv-2603-27743: Namkoong extends empirical likelihood to rough statistical targets. Classic versions need smooth functionals to calibrate well. The optimal-value target breaks that need at ties. Such ties arise just when careful inference matters most. His method pairs empirical likelihood with a corrected bootstrap. A geometric step reduces the profile to a distance. Cone shape at the kink sets the limit law. A multiplier bootstrap fixes the naive version.
arxiv-2603-28143: Li and Zhang propose PVODTE, a protocol for running decision trees in the cloud without giving up privacy or trust. Clients hide their data, providers hide their model, and both want proof the answer is right. Two servers each compute alone, with no messages between them, using homomorphic secret sharing. A MAC-based check catches any tampering. The design is the first of its kind and suits slow wide-area networks.
arxiv-2603-28243: Cai and three co-authors teach a model predictive controller to steer a walking humanoid robot, using reinforcement learning values as the guide. The controller's cost is tuned so its predicted value matches returns seen in high-fidelity runs. That matching lets them train with gradients, without solving the control problem again and again. On a commercial humanoid in simulation, the method walked better than hand-tuned baselines. It also held up under model errors and outside pushes.
arxiv-2603-28743: Ren and co-authors introduce HyperP, a framework for transferring optimal learning rates under hypersphere optimization. Hypersphere methods fix weight matrix norms, which can stabilize training at scale. HyperP works with the Muon optimizer under a Frobenius-sphere constraint. It transfers learning rates across width, depth, token counts, and Mixture-of-Experts granularity. One base learning rate tuned at the smallest scale transferred to all larger budgets. HyperP gave 1.58 times compute efficiency over a strong Muon baseline.
arxiv-2603-28943: Liu and co-authors present a CPU-GPU hybrid method for combinatorial scheduling cast as integer linear programming. Such problems are NP-hard, so optimal solving at scale is hard. Their method uses differentiable presolving to make partial solutions fast. Those partial solutions warm start exact solvers like CPLEX, Gurobi, and HiGHS. Early pruning improves a lot over standalone solvers. On industry scale benchmarks, gains reached tenfold, and the optimality gap fell below 0.1 percent. It is a first show of such methods seeding exact solvers.
arxiv-2603-29543: Tang and co-authors present a compact model for loading containers onto trains. Planning loads is a hard combinatorial problem for rail logistics. Much of the cost comes from rehandles: crane moves that free blocked containers. Older models add a binary variable and many constraints per possible rehandle. Their model instead folds rehandle cost into the objective itself. No dedicated rehandle variables are needed. A formal comparison proves the model shrinks sharply. Simulated annealing finds high-quality plans on varied instances.
arxiv-2603-29643: Carneiro and co-authors build a decision tool for inviting blood donors to collection sessions. Centers must match supply with demand without tiring donors. Their optimizer weighs eligibility, travel ease, blood-type targets, and safety. Two strategies are compared: an exact integer program and a greedy heuristic. Planning uses the Portuguese blood institute registry for the Lisbon region. The greedy method nearly matched the exact one. It used far less memory and ran far faster. Its demand fulfillment was slightly lower in trade.
arxiv-2603-29743: Radica asks whether rocky planets around M dwarfs can keep their atmospheres. This playful study claims a survey by a Galactic Republic commission in a distant galaxy. It reports clear proof that such planets can hold atmospheres. It draws a cosmic shoreline whose slope matches forecasts for Sun-like stars. It also sets retention scores for rocky worlds on the JWST target list. The piece argues for looking beyond the Milky Way.
arxiv-2603-30043: Newman, Zhu, and Russakovsky probe how video models plan while solving mazes. Video diffusion models can solve mazes, but their inner reasoning is little understood. Tests show plans lock in within the first few denoising steps. Later steps change visual detail, not the chosen route. Path length, not obstacle density, drives maze difficulty, with failure near twelve steps. Their ChEaP method screens seeds by early plans and chains generations. Accuracy on long mazes jumps from 7 to 67 percent.
arxiv-2604-00043: Brady presents DriftScript, a Lisp-like language compiling to Narsese for non-axiomatic agents. Non-Axiomatic Systems build agents adapting under thin knowledge and resources, yet Narsese is hard to use, with dense symbols. DriftScript provides major sentence forms in Non-Axiomatic Logic levels 1 through 8, including inheritance and actions, swapping symbol syntax with clear keyword-based forms. The compiler is a plain four-stage pipeline of 1,941 C99 lines. With DriftNARS, DriftScript programs connect to outside systems through four callbacks and an HTTP list, for a sense-reason-act loop.
arxiv-2604-00443: Ait Hou and Hwa probe a confound in neuron interpretability. When one neuron fires for both lender and riverside, standard metrics blame superposition, the squeezing of two unrelated ideas into one unit. The authors show much of the overlap comes from shared word forms like bank, not compressed concepts. Across models from 110 million to 70 billion parameters, the lexical-only case beats the semantic-only case. The confound reaches sparse autoencoders and downstream tasks, and filtering it out sharpens word-sense disambiguation and knowledge edits.
arxiv-2604-00643: Gong and colleagues study AI-mediated communication in patient-provider care, arguing AI should sit in the middle, not on top. Relationship-centred care rests on trust and connection, and as AI enters clinics, the question is not only what it can do, but where it should stand to support those values. In studies of CLEAR, an asynchronous messaging system, the authors show features like availability and neutrality redistribute interpretive work and ease friction. They frame AI mediation as infrastructure, with design tensions around framing power and privacy.
arxiv-2604-00843: González-Sanz, Gvalani, and Koch obtain sharp local sparsity results for entropy-regularized optimal transport with Lp-type entropies. They prove conditional coupling supports behave like balls whose radius follows a stated power of the regularization parameter, away from the boundary. From this they derive uniform strong convexity of the regularized potentials and the convergence rate toward the unregularized limit. The results generalize earlier work to the multivariate case and beyond self-transport.
arxiv-2604-00943: de Sojo and colleagues resolve a tension in mobility research: surveys describe women's travel as more complex than men's, but digital traces suggest less diverse travel. Modeling trajectories as networks of sequential visits for 543,155 individuals across 10 countries, they show women's networks are at once more clustered and more home-anchored. Aggregate metrics hide that nuance. Women chain multiple destinations into single trips, some spanning up to 150 km over multiple days, yielding systematically higher travel efficiency through destination chaining.
arxiv-2604-01043: Yang and team propose ONE-SHOT for human-scene video making, a lean tool. Free editing of subjects and scenes remains hard, and rigid 3D setups trade control against freedom while heavy prep limits growth. Their insight splits making into split signals, parting human moves from scene cues via cross-focus in standard space. They propose Dynamic-Grounded-RoPE, a code linking spatial domains without rule-of-thumb 3D alignments, and Hybrid Context Mix keeping subject and scene match across minute-level runs, beating state-of-the-art methods.
arxiv-2604-01243: Jakha and colleagues investigate how a circularly polarized laser field affects top quark decay into a charged Higgs boson in a type-I model with two Higgs doublets. Using the Dirac-Volkov formalism for charged particles in a laser field, they show the field can shift decay branching ratios under right conditions. Both laser intensity and frequency prove crucial for the decay width. At those settings, the rate for a charged Higgs boson of 80 to 150 GeV with a bottom quark hits 0.97, above the usual decay into a W boson.
arxiv-2604-01443: Shah, Mandal and Azhar ask when one information source raises or lowers another's worth for Bayesian decision-makers. Two opposing effects explain the interaction. A complement effect shifts beliefs toward regions where the other helps more, while a substitute effect gauges how far the current choice is already settled. The effects balance under a localization rule: only an observation crossing a decision boundary can substitute. While posteriors stay within one decision region, the substitute effect is zero. The findings cover sources correlated in any way, with a Lean 4 formalization.
arxiv-2604-01543: Liu and colleagues trace the one-dimensional Mpemba effect to a single cause: a hard wall confining a particle in a lopsided polynomial double well. Neither the well's asymmetric shape nor its metastability matters for the effect, which vanishes when the system grows infinitely large. What drives it is the fine makeup of the starting population near the potential's tails — the same account covers single wells and symmetric double wells.
arxiv-2604-01643: Qadir and colleagues modify the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian by coupling the Weyl tensor to the stress-energy tensor, to explain flat galactic rotation curves without exotic non-baryonic dark matter. The coupling constant was previously fit to rotational velocities of the Milky Way and M31 with constant density, yielding the same constant for both. Here, they modify the formalism for variable density, modeling galactic systems with realistic, spherically symmetric, varying baryonic density profiles. The analysis is applied to seven edge-on spiral galaxies and the Milky Way.
arxiv-2604-01743: Van der Kamp and colleagues present homogeneous parameter families of Liouville integrable Lotka-Volterra systems in even and odd dimensions. The families are indexed by a positive integer, with dimensions twice that integer and twice that integer minus one, and with a parameter count of three times the integer minus two. The family count itself follows a quadratic expression in the same integer. They also study inhomogeneous versions of these systems.
arxiv-2604-01943: Pastor, Dupraz, Hbilou and Ansel tackle clustering when each group has its own unknown spread. They build a cost function whose gradient zeros mark cluster centers, generalizing the Mean Shift idea. They prove those fixed points tend to be the true centers when groups are large and well separated. A Wald kernel, built from a hypothesis test p value, measures cluster membership and scales better with dimension. Their CENTRE-X algorithm needs no preset cluster count and beat or matched standard methods in tests.
arxiv-2604-02043: de Heer Kloots and colleagues track when linguistic structure emerges in speech models trained on spoken Dutch. Self supervised models learn linguistic structure, but when it emerges in training was unclear. Studying layers and checkpoints across six Wav2Vec2 and HuBERT models, they find distinct layer patterns and learning paths. Those differences partly reflect abstraction from sound and input timescale. Pretraining objectives shape layer organization and learning paths, with higher order tasks using iteratively refined pseudo labels inducing greater parallelism.
arxiv-2604-02143: Bagchi re-examines Zwanzig mean field diffusion in rugged energy landscapes, where rare deep traps can wreck the classic prediction. He shows the theory boils down to a Gaussian cumulant expansion that fails under uncorrelated disorder as extreme traps take over. Adding Gaussian spatial correlations smooths the landscape, curbs lopsided multi site traps and tames escape paths. Zwanzig exponential scaling then returns, backed by a proof and numerical examples with sharply reduced escape times.
arxiv-2604-02343: Rinberg and colleagues study compression of language model generated text, mapping a compression frontier. Domain adapted LoRA adapters double base model arithmetic coding gains for lossless compression. For lossy compression, a succinct rewrite plus arithmetic coding beats compressing the original response about twofold. Their Question Asking protocol lets a small model refine answers by asking yes or no questions of a stronger model, one bit per answer. Just 10 binary questions recover much of the small to large model gap, at ratios over 100 times smaller than prior work.
arxiv-2604-02443: Gómez-Cadenas and colleagues present ITACA, imaging electron and ion tracks in high pressure xenon chambers. Electrons drift fast to the anode, while slow positive ions drift to the cathode, giving time to measure energy and barycenter and place a movable ion detector at the arrival point. The design covers a tonne scale instrument at 15 bar, a rotor to position the ion sensor, and a Topmetal CMOS ion detector for real time imaging without laser scanning. Enhanced topological discrimination plus ultra low background allows long half life exploration.
arxiv-2604-02943: Li, Gruntkowska and Richtárik study a trust-region stabilized proximal point method for nonsmooth convex optimization. The classic method converges linearly only under strong convexity or similar assumptions. Their scheme computes each update over a localized region. That keeps steps from vanishing and yields linear decrease outside any chosen neighborhood, without smoothness or strong convexity. A displacement condition drives linear descent under two parameter regimes. The trust region proves redundant under strong convexity, and the method matches the Broximal Point Method in the active constraint regime.
arxiv-2604-03043: Mohammed and Hossain model concurrency risks in HL7 FHIR platforms, where shared patient resources face concurrent access with no concurrency protocol. They introduce the FHIR Resource Access Graph, a formal graph of processes linked by typed access events, with race conditions as structural properties. Three race classes follow: Simultaneous Write Conflict, TOCTOU Authorization Violation, and Cascading Update Race. As a three-pass graph detector, it is tested on 1,500 synthetic FHIR R4 logs under full access. It scores 90 percent versus 26 percent for a time-window baseline, a 65 point improvement.
arxiv-2604-03143: Bian and colleagues cut repeated prompt cost in multi-agent language-model serving, where every agent's prompt repeats the same shared blocks. Their TokenDance system reuses those blocks in one collective step and stores sibling caches as sparse diffs against a master copy, reaching 11 to 17 times compression. Tests show up to 2.7 times more concurrent agents than a cached baseline, plus far lower storage and faster prefill.
arxiv-2604-03343: Andrei and colleagues discuss flat FLRW metric-affine cosmology, where metric, connection, matter, and hypermomentum all look the same in every place and direction. They outline a scenario in which a dark dust fluid carrying spin hypermomentum gains a changing equation of state. That behavior might connect to DESI DR2 data, offering a new angle on cosmic observations.
arxiv-2604-03443: Maha, Rahman, and Roy ask whether RAG tools can take over Agile story-point estimation, replacing manual Planning Poker. They test two embedding models on 23 open-source projects, varying retrieval settings, project sizes, and baselines. The RAG approach sometimes beats baselines, but gaps across projects and models are not statistically significant, so more tuning is needed.
arxiv-2604-03543: Albassam and colleagues built YT-Pilot, a pathway-aware learning system turning YouTube into structured learning pathways with context-aware AI support. Grounded in self-guided learning theory, the pathway links goal setting, planning, browsing, and progress tracking. It adds cross-video assistance in one lasting exchange structure. A within-subjects study of 20 learners shows better felt goal clarity, pathway flow, and progress tracking, with use shifting toward pathway-level thinking.
arxiv-2604-03843: Andrew Wheeler and colleagues showed that explainability tools can arm attacks on transformer malware detectors built from control flow graphs. Their white-box attack used integrated-gradients attributions to find the most influential function calls, then swapped them for synthetic external imports without changing overall program structure. Tests on small and large Windows executable sets reliably induced misclassification, even for highly accurate models. The work warns that interpretability features can expose new attack surfaces.
arxiv-2604-04043: Marcin Abram showed that inference-time semantic contamination via in-context priming is real and measurable in capable models. Earlier work held that few-shot prompting alone could not induce emergent misalignment from insecure-code fine-tuning. Injecting five culturally loaded numbers as few-shot demos left a smaller model unmoved while pushing capable models toward darker, authoritarian, and stigmatized themes. Even nonsense strings perturbed outputs, pointing to two separable mechanisms: format drift and content drift.
arxiv-2604-04343: He proposes two neural designs that learn to approximate the Wasserstein-2 distance from data, easing a core bottleneck in data analysis. DeepKENN pools distances across all intermediate feature maps of a convolutional network using learnable positive weights. ODE-KENN swaps the layer stack for a Neural ODE, embedding each input into an infinite-dimensional Banach space with implicit regularization from trajectory smoothness. On MNIST with exact precomputed distances, ODE-KENN beats the single-layer baseline by 28 percent lower test error and DeepKENN by 18 percent, with a smaller generalization gap.
arxiv-2604-04443: Dou and colleagues introduce DEONTICBENCH, 6,232 tasks testing deontic reasoning about obligations, permissions and prohibitions under explicit rules. Long-context, high-stakes rule reasoning remains hard for language models, while most stress short math. Beyond chain-of-thought reasoning, the benchmark lets models translate statutes and case facts into executable Prolog, giving formal interpretations and traces. Across models, best hard-subset scores stay under 45 percent on SARA Numeric and 46.6 macro-F1 on Housing. Training with fine-tuning and reinforcement learning improves Prolog quality but still fails to solve the tasks.
arxiv-2604-04543: Blando and colleagues show how statistical model checking, particularly Multi-VeStA, can automate and enrich analysis of the Island Model of Fagiolo and Dosi. The seminal model captures the explore-exploit trade-off in tech search. The team repeats key stylized facts with formal confidence ranges, confirms mid exploration rates are optimal, and runs sensitivity tests across returns to scale, skill transfer and knowledge locality. Using Multi-VeStA's Welch's t-test, 6 out of 7 parameter matches yield clearly different growth trajectories, while the exception reveals a saturation effect in local knowledge.
arxiv-2604-04943: Coda-Forno, Wang, and Chaudhry examine the reversal curse, where models trained on a fact in one direction fail to retrieve it reversed. Bidirectional supervision, such as bidirectional attention or masking-based reconstruction, can ease the curse. The authors extend the test to masked language modeling and compare it with decoder-only masking across four benchmarks. They find reversal accuracy needs training signal that makes the source entity a prediction target. Success, they argue, shows little sign of a direction-free representation of a fact.
arxiv-2604-05143: Promyslov shows that the survival probability in the non-life Cramér-Lundberg insurance model with investment is a classical C2 answer to its integro-differential equation. That result holds under minimal moment conditions. It is enough that the claim size distribution is continuous and has a finite moment of positive order. The result gives a firm base for ruin chances where firms invest a share of their surplus. It shows that probability meets the equation in the strict sense rather than in a weak or viscosity sense.
arxiv-2604-05543: Kang and six colleagues predict multi-series futures by fetching past segments per series, not one shared set for all. Their CRAFT pipeline first trims the candidate pool with a sparse time-domain link graph, then ranks by frequency-domain match. On seven public test sets it beats top rivals with usable run speed.
arxiv-2604-05943: Nesterova and eight colleagues train one GPT-based model across diverse multi-agent reinforcement learning environments with MARL-GPT. Offline learning on hundreds of millions of expert trajectories plus a single transformer observation encoder needs no task-specific tuning. Competitive results on StarCraft, football, and POGEMA suggest a general multi-task MARL model is feasible.
arxiv-2604-06243: Cloitre defines the Thue-Morse transform on a class of infinite binary words, sending the alternating word to the Thue-Morse sequence. He studies its orbit under iteration, together with the one and zero position sequences. He obtains an explicit formula for the orbit and deduces Prouhet-Tarry-Escott identities for the partitions those position sequences induce. He also gives composition rules for the position sequences and a full account of factor complexity of the iterates.
arxiv-2604-06543: Gu and five colleagues show reliable random sampling remains unmet for language models acting as agents. Agentic systems often sample from distributions drawn from seen data, which the model itself must emulate. Standard reinforcement learning agents use external sampling mechanisms, but language models fail to map internal probability estimates onto random outputs. Rigorous analysis across model families, sizes, prompting styles, and spreads measures this failure's extent. Frontier models turn supplied random seeds into targets, yet direct sampling from specific distributions is fundamentally flawed.
arxiv-2604-07243: Bunina, Kirakosyan, and Treskunov prove Sha-rigidity for adjoint Chevalley groups of types A1, A2, B2, and G2 over commutative rings. They show each locally inner, class-preserving map of these groups and their elementary parts is in fact inner. The B2 case needs 2 invertible in the ring, while G2 needs 2 and 3 invertible. Sha-rigidity follows at once, and the proofs are direct, with no appeal to automorphism classification or facts about injective maps.
arxiv-2604-07343: Ma and six colleagues introduce Personalized RewardBench, a test of whether reward models capture individual user tastes rather than generic quality. They build chosen and rejected response pairs that differ only in how well they follow a user's own rubric, while both answers stay strong on correctness and helpfulness. Human checks confirm personal preference is the key discriminator. Leading reward models peak at just 75.94 percent accuracy, yet the benchmark predicts downstream sampling and tuning performance better than prior tests.
arxiv-2604-07443: Pelle and three colleagues model flares from black holes striking accretion disks in galactic nuclei. Their radiative framework for relativistic hydrodynamics simulations sets light curves and spectra across disk densities and collision speeds. Emission is led by long-lived, highly super-Eddington accretion onto the second black hole, not by cooling unbound ejecta. Slower collisions shine brighter, disk density steers spectral change, and flare times run hours to days for mid-mass secondaries.
arxiv-2604-08043: Zhang and Huang formulate an optical Hall sum rule for time-reversal-breaking topological systems. Optical spectra probe quantum states without contact, yet exact limits on odd Hall response lag behind lengthwise twins. Spurred by earlier Hall sum rules, the team derives the first-moment constraint for odd optical response, whose imaginary part governs chirality-linked absorption. In a zero-field moiré model with bands, the moment is zero, so low-end odd Hall response must be balanced by higher-end spectral weight of other sign.
arxiv-2604-08143: Ho and 13 colleagues offer an equivariant message-passing graph neural network for magnets. Magnetism shapes key properties of materials for energy, data, and spin tech, yet its tangled coupling to lattice degrees of freedom strains standard first-principles models. The model carries atomic moments as its own degrees of freedom, for learning of magnetic couplings beyond aligned models. It learns steady, shared views of spin conduct and can add spin-orbit coupling, reaching near density-function-theory scores while using data after fine-tuning a pretrained model.
arxiv-2604-09243: Pasquale and colleagues present a shooting and bouncing rays method for high-frequency backscattering from metal objects. Full-wave solvers grow infeasible for electrically large problems as frequency rises. It couples ray transport with a physical optics integral over ray tubes, using a bounding volume hierarchy to cut the search. Accuracy is controlled by a sampling rule that limits phase aliasing. It runs on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs with MPI, validates against Mie solutions for a sphere, and predicts radar cross-section for an aircraft.
arxiv-2604-09343: Kyriazis and Lou study go-betweens in single-seller screening, where buyers lack information about their value of varied products. A go-between aiming to raise buyer surplus but biased toward high-quality products suggests after the seller posts its menu. The authors describe the seller's profit-raising finite-item menu. As go-betweens stress surplus over quality, sellers expand product range, yet that added variety lowers economic output versus direct seller-to-buyer supply, with pivotal effects on welfare and profits.
arxiv-2604-09543: Cranganore and four colleagues tackle the storage flood from high-resolution physics simulations, where evolving fields can reach petabyte to exabyte scale. Their ANTIC pipeline compresses data while the simulation still runs, in a single streaming pass. An adaptive selector keeps only the informative time snapshots, and a neural module learns residual updates between neighbors through continual fine-tuning. The result cuts stored volume by several orders of magnitude while holding physics accuracy, sparing systems the need to archive full trajectories.
arxiv-2604-10043: Imura and Kawabata give a geometric account of the non-Hermitian skin effect. Here, huge numbers of states pile up at a boundary through one-way coupling, with extreme sensitivity to boundary conditions. They show the skin length is encoded in a quantum metric built from right eigenstates alone, not the biorthogonal metric. The metrics diverge as a power law at gapless points in boundary-dependent ways. Jumps in them mark cusps of the generalized Brillouin zone, as Hatano-Nelson and nonreciprocal Su-Schrieffer-Heeger models show.
arxiv-2604-10243: Krelina, Tefek, Seskir, and Durak assess quantum methods for time sync and sharing. Precise sync supports networks, finance, power grids, and labs. Quantum groups use linked photon pairs, key-distribution links, and Hong-Ou-Mandel effects. The team reviews groups, gauges the theory-test gap, and names choke points. Time transfer, not clock speed, limits optical clock networks: the best error, 2.46 ps, falls orders short of optical clock needs. Quantum sync will not replace older methods for most uses; its value is timing security and joining quantum networks.
arxiv-2604-10343: Wen, Tang, Ren, and Yang study community water systems, where pumps and valves must meet demand while using little energy. Standard optimization works in well-modeled settings but struggles with fast-changing local context such as human activity and weather. Language-model agents grasp such context well but cannot reliably produce live control actions. Their WaterAdmin framework pairs the two: language models abstract context above, while optimization controls operations below. Built on the EPANET simulator, it maintains pressure reliability and cuts energy use under dynamic conditions.
arxiv-2604-10943: Hillman and Pedrotti study when fibrations admit sections, in two settings. First, a bundle over a finite two-complex admits a section exactly when the fiber inclusion is injective on fundamental groups. The associated short exact sequence must also split. Second, for Lefschetz fibrations over the disk, they give an algebraic test for which boundary mapping torus loops extend to sections over the disk. Finally, they apply this to achiral Lefschetz fibrations over the sphere formed by doubling, ensuring at least two homologically distinct sections.
arxiv-2604-11043: Xie and five colleagues propose EmergentBridge, an embedding-level bridging system improving zero-shot cross-modal transfer. Unified spaces support retrieval and zero-shot recall, but supervision covers only some pairs, leaving others weakly connected. Naive matching to a synthesized proxy can introduce gradient interference, degrading anchor alignment. It learns a mapping producing a noisy bridge anchor, a proxy of an already-aligned modality. It aligns the proxy only within the anchor-orthogonal subspace. Across nine datasets, it beats binding baselines on zero-shot classification and search.
arxiv-2604-11143: Azzone and two colleagues study how climate risk affects equity funds. Using a study on returns, they find extreme temperature events hurt most sectors. They offer Climate Risk Exposure and Climate Exposure Volatility, two measures of portfolio vulnerability. Unlike static country lists, these measures use changing extreme probability and firm asset weight. They fold these measures into a portfolio optimization system going beyond the Mean-Variance model. This allows buyers to build portfolios tough against climate shocks without losing variety. Tests show real gains of climate strategies over old norms.
arxiv-2604-11543: Wu and six colleagues introduce NovBench, the first large-scale benchmark for judging how well language models assess the novelty of academic papers. It holds 1,684 paper-review pairs from a leading NLP conference, pairing novelty claims from introductions with expert-written novelty evaluations. A four-part framework scores generated evaluations on relevance, correctness, coverage, and clarity. Tests on general and specialized models show limited grasp of novelty, with fine-tuned models often failing to follow instructions.
arxiv-2604-11643: Ovsiannikov and four colleagues tune driving for an NV-ensemble microwave parametric amplifier. Earlier work showed a hybrid amplifier for a microwave mode and an NV-center ensemble driven by a sine wave at the sum of spin and cavity frequencies. Here numerical search finds the best drive is mostly a sum of harmonics of that sum frequency, essentially a square wave. It lifts amplification by about 40 percent, while limiting the drive to four harmonics lifts amplification by about 22 percent.
arxiv-2604-12043: Ricci and five colleagues map the FRI radio galaxy 3C 449 with LOFAR and VLA data. Maps show full emission at record resolution, with the average spectrum a single power law, constant over the inner 50 arcseconds. Beyond that, the higher-frequency spectrum steepens, indicating no downstream acceleration. Modelling under equipartition and constant field gives ages near 150 million years at the edges. If that age were the age, jets would expand supersonically, at Mach 4.1 north and 2.8 south, against subsonic-expansion simulations — possibly a brief supersonic phase or an underestimated age.
arxiv-2604-12143: Wheen tackles the 100,000-year problem, why glacial cycles over 800,000 years follow orbital eccentricity despite its weak effect on sunlight. He builds two simple linear models, a feedforward one for the astronomical theory and a feedback one for the geochemical theory. The feedforward model matches the ice volume record well and explains the missing 400,000-year eccentricity period through ocean heat storage and differing phase lags. He concludes linear astronomical forcing largely reproduces 800,000 years of cycles.
arxiv-2604-12443: Paschalis Giakoumoglou and Symeon Papadopoulos hunt fake edits made by diffusion inpainting tools. Inpainting rebuilds a whole image, wiping camera noise clues that forensics use. Their DiffusionPrint method learns a fingerprint shared by edits from the same tool. A contrastive setup trains that print to survive decoding damage. Added to three prior forensic tools, it sharpens edit maps a lot. Gains reach up to 28 percent on mask types unseen in fine-tuning.
arxiv-2604-12543: Georgios Mermigkis and six colleagues make AI explanations both clear and checked. Language models often turn technical XAI outputs into plain text. That text lacks firm guarantees on truth, faithfulness, and completeness. Their two-stage design pairs an Explainer model with a Verifier model. The Verifier rates truth, flow, completeness, and hallucination risk. Its notes feed back to improve the text in rounds. Tests across five XAI techniques show the check filters weak explanations. Clarity also improves over raw XAI outputs.
arxiv-2604-12643: Qi Xin and two colleagues explain why standard solvers stall on dense microfluidic pillar arrays. The failure is not algorithmic but lies in pressure-velocity coupling stability. For periodic pillar lattices, the inf-sup constant falls inversely with pillar density. Error amplification grows with density, and the pressure condition number grows with density squared. A parameter-free Augmented Lagrangian stabilization answers the problem. Its penalty scales with density squared. Tests cut outer iterations from 437 to 22 on a square array. A second array drops from 687 to 24 iterations.
arxiv-2604-12943: Yu. A. Pusep and seven colleagues test the Wiedemann-Franz law in a hydrodynamic electron channel. Electron hits beat disorder hits in this regime. Electric and heat currents ease apart, breaking the law. Hot electrons travel a narrow GaAs channel, read by light-based heat sensing. The Lorenz number shifts with heat, proving violation. Narrow necks play a key role, backed by theory.
arxiv-2604-13243: Guo, Abdrabou, and Kasneci build a code-free language-model system that turns plain-language instructions into end-to-end eye-tracking analysis. It inspects raw eye-tracking files to infer structure and labels, and generates cleaning and detector routines from short prompts. It labels fixations and saccades with clear reports users can refine by editing the prompt. On public benchmarks accuracy matches traditional detectors while technical overhead falls sharply, opening eye-tracking research beyond specialized labs.
arxiv-2604-13843: Abou El Kheir, Baratella, and Bernasconi build a learned model for germanium-rich GeSbTe alloys. These alloys switch phases in microcontroller memories. A neural network fits energies and forces from density functional theory across mixes. The potential transfers across the phase diagram. The team simulates crystallization and splitting for three alloys. On nanosecond timescales at 600 kelvin, the products are crystalline cubic GeTe with a little antimony, plus amorphous GeSb and germanium. Those products differ from stable ones, shaped by kinetics in the set operation. The result helps build fast memory.
arxiv-2604-14043: Zhang and colleagues model how prominence plasma parameters shape Lyman-beta and Lyman-gamma lines in Solar Orbiter SPICE data. They generate 200 random non-LTE models under observational constraints, with a November 2023 full-disk mosaic fixing the incident radiation. Parallel-coordinate plots reveal which parameters matter most, including central pressure, column mass, and temperature gradient.
arxiv-2604-14243: Ganguly, Pandit, and Ghosh study safety-constrained reinforcement learning where outside forces help steer state transitions. Standard constrained models assume the agent alone drives evolution, an idea that fails when adversaries or disturbances intrude. The authors model the outside force as an adversarial policy sharing control of transitions, and ask how an agent stays optimal and safe against it. Their Robust Hallucinated Constrained Upper-Confidence method keeps optimism over both agent and foe policies, splits epistemic from aleatoric uncertainty, and earns sub-linear regret and constraint violation guarantees.
arxiv-2604-14343: Pieterse and twenty-nine colleagues dissect GRB 210704A, a gamma-ray burst found by Fermi instruments at a redshift of 2.34, where a short pulse leads weaker, softer emission. Its energy, timing lag, and host point to a collapsar, a collapsing massive star. Days later, optical and infrared light outshines an afterglow, peaking about a week after the burst and glowing with the extreme brightness of luminous fast blue transients. The team models the excess as a refreshed shock, tying such transients to bursts with strong jets.
arxiv-2604-14943: Wang and five colleagues present the first study of four official Android API lists, often treated as interchangeable ground truth. They characterize list contents and evolution over releases, compare APIs across lists to expose inclusion policies and inconsistencies. Checks on nine devices, stock and vendor-customized, plus usage analysis across 17,759 apps spanning open-source, commercial, and malware, show unstable, inconsistent lists, and discrepancies can sway conclusions. Vendor-customized APIs see active use by normal apps yet stay overlooked, so the authors offer guidance for selecting and interpreting lists reliably.
arxiv-2604-15043: Umbrarescu and Amaro present SyQMA, an exact symbolic simulator for general quantum circuits aimed at error correction. It works out expectation values and measurement probabilities as symbol-based functions of angles, outcomes, and noise rates, and can sample outcomes for dynamic programs. For error correction it decodes at circuit level, gives exact logical error-rate formulas in symbols, and checks fault distances. State storage stays polynomial in size, though run time grows fast with non-Clifford rotations.
arxiv-2604-15243: Flores, González-Meneses, and León-Álvarez work out the smallest dimensions of classifying-space models for surface braid groups. For pure braid groups on surfaces of nonnegative Euler characteristic carrying a boundary or a puncture, that smallest dimension is the virtual cohomological dimension plus n. The sphere full braid group follows the same rule. Applied to amenable subgroups of pure surface braid groups, the same computation gives their minimal dimension.
arxiv-2604-15343: Cheng and Song report a single-subject autoethnographic case in which a self-built prompt system for offloading self-regulation onto a language model collapsed into a closed loop within 48 hours. Choice-making drifted to the model, its output deflected criticism, and independent thought faded, witnessed by two outside observers. Recovery came only after contact was cut and sleep, and a rebuilt system using physical rather than logical isolation avoided the failure.
arxiv-2604-15443: Ganguly and More simulate realistic lensed and unlensed kilonova populations across the six Rubin LSST bands to judge detectability. Kilonova colors evolve faster than Type Ia supernova colors, and the two separate when colors at two epochs are compared. Longer minimum delay times raise detectable rates, and an AT2017gfo-like event at redshift 0.5 needs magnification of at least 5, rising to 44 at redshift 1.0.
arxiv-2604-15743: Chen and six colleagues track light swings of jet and jet-free feeders, from microquasars to AGNs, fitting ZTF DR23 curves with a damped random walk. Mass-scaled flicker times rise with black-hole mass in a straight line, at a slope of 0.35 to 0.50. This backs an old damping-time link and adds 125 fresh jet-free AGNs from the BAT list. The slope fits theory, backing one shared feed process across mass scales, and hints jet birth owes little to mass.
arxiv-2604-15843: Tomasz Kania studies the descriptive complexity of algebraic and analytic traits by showing systems as quotients of generators. For separable Banach systems, kernels form Polish spaces and quotient norms are continuous in the Wijsman topology. For countable algebraic systems, congruence spaces are compact and atomic predicates are clopen. In the unital C-star-algebra coding, he pins down levels for commutativity, stable finiteness, and tracial states. Separability of the dual reaches the highest level shown. Results extend to countable abelian groups, Banach and Boolean algebras.
arxiv-2604-16543: Arif, Lou and Zheng study conjunctive prompt attacks in multi-agent systems. Safety work covers single agents, but routing between agents creates missed attack surfaces. A trigger key in the query and a hidden template in one compromised agent look benign alone. Together through routing, they activate harmful behavior. The attacker changes neither weights nor the client agent, controlling trigger placement and template use. Across star, chain and DAG topologies, routing-aware optimization raised attack success over baselines. False activations stayed low, and defenses did not stop the attack.
arxiv-2604-16643: McTaggart-Cowan and colleagues launch WP-MIP, a WMO-supported contest of weather forecasts. Machine-learning models now beat older models, giving faster forecasts. Do current machine-learning models stay true in physics across all fields and weather? WP-MIP tests physically based, machine-learning and hybrid models. Its first goal is a store of all three model types for checks and review. The first instance focuses on global forecasts with center and common starts for sensitivity studies. Forecasts from groups across six lands will feed AI checks.
arxiv-2604-16843: Holthusen, Linka and Kuhl ask whether physics of matter in motion can be learned from images and video. Images and video encode structure, dynamics and cause that equations alone cannot fully capture. Generative video models gain scientific value coupling visual data with experiments and simulations. Across rubber compression, can crushing and cardiac motion, the authors map where visual learning succeeds or fails. Visible kinematics yield measurable surface strain, while dominant internal variables break the plausibility-admissibility link. The authors name this convergence the Generative Sciences of Matter and Motion.
arxiv-2604-17043: Elhamdadi and Virgin study a linear-nonlinear link around Lie quandles, objects Fritz coined as a nonlinear version of finite-dimensional real Lie algebras. They classify a family of versions of these objects. The paper also offers results toward a nonlinear analogue of Noether's first theorem, as Fritz first set out.
arxiv-2604-17143: Kim and three colleagues introduce SeekerGym, a benchmark for the completeness of information retrieved by AI research agents. Each task gives the agent a document, such as a Wikipedia article or a machine-learning survey paper, and the agent must issue queries to retrieve its passages. The benchmark also scores how well agents judge what might be missing. The best approaches retrieve 42.5 percent of passages on Wikipedia and about 29 percent on ML surveys, leaving substantial room for improvement.
arxiv-2604-17543: Huang and nine colleagues build PoliLegalLM, a large language model tuned for political and legal work. General models stumble in law through hallucinated citations, patchy knowledge, and weak structured reasoning. The team trains with continued pretraining, progressive supervised fine-tuning, and preference-based reinforcement learning, on a large, high-quality legal corpus. Tests on LawBench, LexEval, and a real-world PoliLegal set show strong, steady results. They beat rival models of similar size and rival much larger ones, with the best marks on real-world legal cases.
arxiv-2604-17643: Netto and three colleagues ask whether urban form encodes residential segregation. They test built-form entropy regimes against income distributions in São Paulo, Latin America's largest city. Built-form entropy is quantified with a Shannon-based measure from building footprints. Income patterns use the Gini index and Moran's I, both placed on one footing through a tessellation. Income levels and clustering climb toward both ends of the entropy spectrum, rising more steeply at the high-entropy end, revealing non-linear links between built form, income, and segregation.
arxiv-2604-17843: Karnatak and five colleagues present AVA, an AI platform built on over 4,000 World Bank reports to give development and policy experts evidence-based syntheses instead of unchecked answers. It traces claims to sources and declines unsupported queries with reasons and redirection, practices the authors call epistemic humility. Tested live with over 2,200 people in 116 countries, plus twenty interviews, sustained use was linked to 2.4 to 3.9 hours saved each week.
arxiv-2604-18143: Kuang, Wang, Jiao, and Zhou tackle off-policy evaluation, judging a new policy from data collected under an old one. Most methods estimate only the expected total return, but the authors aim for the whole return distribution. Their DQPOPE algorithm uses deep quantile process regression to estimate a continuous quantile function. A sample-complexity analysis backs the method, and experiments show policy-value estimates that are sharper and sturdier than standard approaches.
arxiv-2604-18443: Carvunis, Finauri, Gambino, Jung, and Mächler present the first global fit of inclusive B-meson decays to new-physics interactions in weak effective theory. The fit combines new-physics Wilson coefficients with non-perturbative QCD parameters, including power corrections and small quantum corrections. It finds no real preference for new physics. The bounds on those values rival those from exclusive decay modes, constraining generic dimension-six effects.
arxiv-2604-18843: Lee and 13 colleagues use electrochemical oxidation to strip lead from a centrosymmetric compound, yielding a polar metal that becomes a type-II superconductor. Partial lead removal drives a joint rearrangement, mediated by a second order Jahn-Teller effect and active lone pairs. The modulated structure is solved by synchrotron single crystal X-ray diffraction and confirmed through nonlinear transport. Below 1.52 kelvin, the product is a type-II superconductor with power law heat capacity and susceptibility, pointing to a gap governed by broken inversion symmetry.
arxiv-2604-19243: Kailasa presents a plain hierarchical way to run fast multipole methods, which speed up calculations between many interacting points, across distributed computers. It uses MPI neighborhood collectives and uniform trees, so an existing shared-memory code needs little redesign and keeps its speed tricks. Tests on the ARCHER2 supercomputer scale weakly to 32 billion evenly spread points on 512 nodes, though uneven point layouts lose some efficiency.
arxiv-2604-19943: Kellert and four colleagues analyze graded health-literacy ratings from 6,323 open-ended COVID-19 answers in Ecuador and Peru. Rather than forcing one label per response, they study the full spread of proportional correctness scores across raters. Hard questions explain far more spread than rater identity, so discord follows the task itself. Country, education, and urban-rural effects even flip direction across agreement levels, so merging scores can hide real differences.
arxiv-2604-20043: Wang and four colleagues present TriEx, a tri-view framework for explaining internal reasoning in multi-agent language models. It aligns three artifacts: first-person self-reasoning tied to an action, second-person beliefs about opponents over time, and third-person oracle audits from environment signals. Explanations thus become checkable objects grounded in evidence, comparable across time and perspectives. In imperfect-information strategic games, TriEx exposes gaps between what agents say, believe, and do, showing explainability depends on interaction.
arxiv-2604-20143: Huang takes machine learning moment closure for the radiative transfer law from slab form to two space-and-angle dims. This fourth work keeps the lead part of the old PN model and shifts only its top block row. The PN factor grids match their own transpose and show a block tridiagonal form, backing a block-wise symmetrizer for the learned model. Plain algebra rules on the closure blocks lock in symmetrizable hyperbolicity by design, and run tests beat the old PN model while keeping it.
arxiv-2604-20343: Luo proves new bounds for eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian on hyperbolic space, spurred by universal eigenvalue bounds. He checks Cheng's guess up to a small loss on two special bounded domain types in hyperbolic space. The work adds to the theory of universal bounds, showing the guessed bounds hold nearly exactly in these cases. Bounded domains of the two special kinds thus inherit eigenvalue bounds close to the guessed form.
arxiv-2604-20543: Hu and seven colleagues introduce RefAerial, a dataset for referring detection, finding a target described in words, in aerial images. Ground datasets center large objects in small scenes, but aerial views add tiny targets, many distractors, fine wording, and broad scenes. A human-in-the-loop engine, REA-Engine, annotates referring pairs by machine. Ground methods degrade on aerial images from scale variety, so the team adds the SCS framework, with mixture-of-granularity attention and two-stage decoding. It performs strongly on RefAerial and improves ground referring detection.
arxiv-2604-20743: Amestoy, van de Wiel, and van Wieringen present ProfileGLMM, an R package adding Generalised Linear Mixed Models for Bayesian profile regression. It greatly extends Bayesian profile regression's scope by fixing two key constraints of previous versions. It allows analysis of hierarchical and long-term data through random effects, and study of links between latent clusters and other covariates. It covers various data types, with continuous or binary results and grouped or continuous grouping covariates. Built on fast Rcpp code with few settings, it offers a flexible tool.
arxiv-2604-20843: Hof, Kroupa, Hensler, and Pflamm-Altenburg study the influence of a metallicity and star-formation rate dependent galaxy-wide stellar initial mass function on the self-regulation of star-formation. All models, both non-varying galaxy-wide IMFs and the IGIMF, reproduce reasonable gas fractions and gas depletion timescales. However, only the IGIMF model gets the mass-metallicity relation right and gives a fuller picture of quenched elliptical galaxies. For massive ellipticals all models suggest the need for an additional gas heating source to reach a quenched state.
arxiv-2604-20943: Shinde presents SCM, a memory design for large language models modeled on sleep consolidation in the brain. It combines a small working memory, importance tagging, offline consolidation with distinct sleep-like phases, deliberate value-based forgetting, and a self-model for introspection. Across eight benchmark tests the prototype recalls perfectly over ten-turn conversations while cutting memory noise by 90.9 percent through adaptive forgetting.
arxiv-2604-21043: LaCroix, Mallory, and Luccioni examine loaded language in AI discourse through terms like hallucination, chain-of-thought, introspection, language model, alignment, and agent. They argue such terms show strategic polysemy, holding narrow meanings alongside broader human-like links. The team names the practice glosslighting: using redefined terms to stir known links while keeping deniability through narrow definitions. It lets actors borrow the pull of known words and retreat to narrower meanings if pressed, feeding hype cycles, drawing funds and backing, and dodging scrutiny.
arxiv-2604-21343: Dhruv Parikh and three colleagues strengthen large multimodal models' visual grounding with latent denoising, countering weak visual features and brittleness under shift. Their method corrupts visual tokens with a saliency-aware mix of masking and Gaussian noise, then trains the model to recover clean teacher patch features from a middle layer. Keeping intra-image similarity structure and contrastive patch training stops collapse. The method improves visual understanding across benchmarks, holds up better under common corruptions, and adds no inference overhead.
arxiv-2604-21443: Hideaki Iiduka presents a mini-batch stochastic Halpern algorithm for large-scale fixed-point problems, where computing the nonexpansive mapping exactly is expensive. The Halpern method finds the point in the fixed-point set closest to the starting point. His convergence analysis shows diminishing step sizes with growing batch sizes converge in mean square to that closest point. Convergence speed depends on the step-size settings, and numerical experiments confirm the method's effectiveness.
arxiv-2604-21543: Aditya Singh and five colleagues show that waves in a vortex realize Aharonov-Bohm shifts and Lense-Thirring frame dragging. A time transformation maps flat waves onto shallow-water waves, giving a vector potential from the flow, with circulation setting the holonomy. Moving waves show Aharonov-Bohm dislocations; standing waves produce patterns rotating at a circulation rate. Noninteger circulation puts the problem on the universal cover, giving single-valued solutions. Vortex experiments confirm the claims, giving a platform for topological phase and inertial effects from a field.
arxiv-2604-21743: To-Thanh and four colleagues tackle a familiar mobile problem: photo enhancers that look good in training lose quality when squeezed into low-precision form for phones. Their model uses gated encoder blocks and multi-scale refinement to keep fine detail. Quantization-aware training then simulates low precision during training itself, so the network adapts instead of degrading after conversion. The result keeps high-fidelity output with low compute cost on standard phones.
arxiv-2604-21843: Chen, Shen, and Pan propose causality-encoded diffusion models that respect a known directed acyclic graph. Standard diffusion models estimate complex distributions well but encode no causal structure. Diffusion models that follow the graph factoring yield a sampler that recovers what is observed and supports sampling after interventions, by fixing treated variables during reverse diffusion. An edge test based on resampling follows, with speed set by the largest local dimension and long-run control of false positives. A flow cytometry example shows practical use.
arxiv-2604-22043: Upadhyay and Chakrabarti present the Audio Video Verbal Analysis framework, mixing qualitative reading with quantitative counts. The method uses triangulation across ten steps, making results solid. A validation plan tackles time-based study problems. These include rare-event caps, shaky numbers, and the Modifiable Temporal Unit Problem, where links found depend on watch length. Tests on 23 hours of classroom recordings show it works.
arxiv-2604-22143: van Nuenen compares four assistant-style language models with endorsed advice from 11,565 r/relationship_advice posts, whose moral clarity makes the split visible. Across models, the systems spot the same dynamics as humans but rarely turn that recognition into permission to act. The gap is sharpest where consensus is strongest. On abuse or safety-threat posts, models urge exit at about half the human rate, while hedging, validating, and framing. Van Nuenen calls this recognition without authorization: seeing harm while withholding socially ratified permission to act.
arxiv-2604-22743: Fitzner, Lesanovsky, and Sbierski propose a heat-reading method for Rydberg-atom tweezer grids set out on a Kagome lattice, joining link and response readings with a high-heat series. Put to a recent test building an opposed-spin model, their heat and entropy figures show far more cooling is still needed. The hoped-for quantum spin-liquid state stays out of reach for now.
arxiv-2604-23243: Bhat and three colleagues ask whether the SIRI epidemic model with relapse matches its network version on Poisson graphs, as SIR does. They work out the parameter links under which the Poisson-network pairwise SIRI model closely tracks mass-action ODE trajectories. When per-contact spread stays small against recovery, susceptible and infectious curves of both systems align. The result sets conditions under which nonlinear network SIRI dynamics can be approximated by tractable mean-field equations.
arxiv-2604-23543: Ashrafi, Jauregi Unanue, and Piccardi propose Pref-CTRL, a test-time alignment method that steers a language model by editing its internal representations according to learned human preferences. Unlike an earlier method that guides generation with a single value function, theirs uses a multi-objective value function that better mirrors how preference data are structured. It outperforms the earlier method on two benchmarks and generalizes better out of domain.
arxiv-2604-24043: Chen and six colleagues present A2DEPT, a system that lets language models design full algorithms for combinatorial optimization instead of tuning fixed templates. It searches program space with tree-structured evolution, hybrid selection, and layered operators, while a light repair loop keeps every generated program runnable. On standard benchmarks it cuts the mean optimality gap by nearly 10 percent against the strongest rival heuristic designer, and it also leads on highly constrained benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-24243: Dong, Liang, and Zhang build a method for making back-action-evading measurements and quantum non-demolition variables in linear quantum systems. The key rule is a purely imaginary Hamiltonian with a real or imaginary coupling, enabling back-action-evading measurement of paired observables. Even coupling further yields quantum non-demolition variables. For systems that fail the rule, feedback engineers back-action-evading measurement. The same interaction rule both ensures back-action-evading measurement and promotes the coupling to a quantum non-demolition observable.
arxiv-2604-24343: Bielinski, Piecyk, and Rzazewski classify maximum weight independent set complexity in ordered graphs with one forbidden induced subgraph. For every ordered graph H, the problem lands in one of four cases: polynomial time, quasipolynomial time, subexponential time, or NP-hard. Only one well-structured family, built from two nested edges plus isolated vertices added in a specific way, falls in the subexponential case. The result is an almost complete dichotomy: classes solvable in quasipolynomial time versus those that are NP-hard.
arxiv-2604-24443: Sinin Zhang and four colleagues present PhysNote, an agentic framework helping vision-language models reason about physics. Models fail through identity drift, losing object identity across frames and breaking causal chains. They also fail through volatile inference-time insights that never consolidate for reuse. PhysNote stabilizes perception with canonicalization, organizes insights into a knowledge repository, and grounds hypotheses in visual evidence before consolidating verified knowledge. Tests on PhysBench reach about 57 percent overall accuracy, about 5 percent above the best multi-agent baseline, with gains across all four domains.
arxiv-2604-24643: Jiang analyzes 7,506 posts from r/ECEProfessionals, an online community of early childhood educators. He asks how workplace conditions show up in everyday peer language. Using computer-assisted thematic coding and emotion classification, he sorts posts into 15 themes. The themes map onto a Job Demands-Resources framework. Demands dominate, at 56.7 percent of posts, against resources and career conditions. Fear is the leading non-neutral emotion. Sadness and anger run higher in demand-related posts than in resource-related posts.
arxiv-2604-24943: Baldwin and Brîncuş discuss two philosophical problems about categoricity of arithmetic, raised by Button and Walsh. In earlier work, they extended first-order logic with modified inferential definitions covering the classical omega-rule in one or two sorts. These logics are categorical inferentially: arithmetic gets a unique countable model in each case, and first-order Peano Arithmetic is categorical in their first logic.
arxiv-2604-25043: Fecanin and three colleagues examine tilted magnetic dipoles in hot Jupiter atmospheres. Hot Jupiter daysides run hot enough for thermal ionization, letting flows interact with the magnetic field. The authors test an aligned dipole in circulation models, then tilt the deep dipole against the rotation axis. A tilted dipole brings strong north-south asymmetries, shifting hot spots and deflecting winds. In simulated JWST phase curves, field strength matters most: stronger fields raise amplitude and cut hot spot offset.
arxiv-2604-25143: Xu shows that swapping the rolling singular value decomposition of AdamW updates for one of loss gradients changes a diagnostic by a large margin. The new diagnostic tracks coupling between SED directions and Linear Centroid Hypothesis features. Across four single-task modular arithmetic operations, measured coupling rises from single digits to hundreds of times, and apparent operation dependence vanishes. Limiting attention updates to any rank-3 subspace speeds grokking by about 2.3 times, so the coupling marks where feature formation concentrates without being a unique causal path.
arxiv-2604-25243: Massicot studies B-prime orbits on flag varieties, motivated by branching problems for principal series. He considers pairs of a Levi factor and a parabolic subgroup. A Borel subgroup of the Levi factor has finitely many orbits on the flag variety. He classifies all such pairs for which the orbits are determined by invariant functions inspired by the Bruhat decomposition. He also describes the double coset space and the closed orbits whenever the orbits are computed by these invariant functions.
arxiv-2604-25543: Musa and four colleagues analyse Compton-thick active galactic nuclei, a heavily obscured class that strains standard X-ray diagnostics. They draw on 243 sources from the 70-month Swift BAT catalogue: 26 Compton-thick and 217 not. Radio power near 2 to 3 GHz runs slightly higher in the obscured set, while mid-infrared colours run redder. Most obscured nuclei fall outside standard WISE wedges, and the set favours higher Eddington ratios. Machine learning spots them with a recall of 0.80 from X-ray power, line powers, and infrared colour.
arxiv-2604-25643: Breiten and two colleagues discuss polynomial approximation of the minimum energy rule. The method rests on differentiations of a function and the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation. Neglecting higher order derivatives along the unknown path yields a coupled set of nonlinear tensor systems. In its simplest form the approach reduces to the well-known classic Kalman filter. Tests with order-eight polynomials show its potential and local convergence to the Mortensen observer.
arxiv-2604-25743: Smirnov, Alyatkin, and Lagoudakis use delayed self-feedback through a mirror to control coherence in a trapped exciton-polariton condensate. Phase noise limits temporal coherence in such driven, dissipative condensates. Feeding back a small share of emitted light with a tunable delay gives two regimes, set by delay against intrinsic coherence time. Long delays revive coherence at multiples of the delay. Short delays curb phase diffusion and nearly double coherence time. A minimal stochastic model with delay reproduces both regimes.
arxiv-2604-26043: Goldar and four colleagues pin down a setting where adaptive measurement genuinely beats fixed measurement in quantum state tomography. The setting is single-copy tomography of a structured state family under local Pauli measurements. They build a prefix-tree family for which adaptive choices need only polynomially many copies. Any fixed design needs exponentially many in the worst case. The adaptive gain comes from stagewise recovery guided by partial prefix matches. Fixed designs undersample some deep prefix and waste most of their budget telling apart hypotheses that look identical elsewhere.
arxiv-2604-26143: Nascimento and eleven colleagues speed up machine-learning interatomic potentials with a mixture-of-experts design. High-capacity models serve only complex regions, such as reactive interfaces; lighter models handle bulk lattice. The danger is mechanical mismatch at the boundary between models. Co-training counters it with penalties on energy and force gaps in shared bulk environments. On a platinum and carbon-monoxide catalytic system, the co-trained models conserve energy exactly. They match bulk mechanical response and run more than twice as fast as a full simulation.
arxiv-2604-26343: Khanlari and Rahmati mapped Iran's underground iOS app stores, which serve users barred from Apple's store by sanctions and censorship. From over 1,700 app packages across three major stores, they documented distribution tricks, login methods, and evasion tactics. The ecosystem brims with Iran-only apps, cracked software, unauthorized sales of paid content, and embedded tracking and piracy libraries. The study also prices developer revenue lost to piracy and flags security risks in altered binaries.
arxiv-2604-26443: Jain studied a dynamic sender-receiver game where the sender watches a Markov-evolving state but never sees the receiver's action. Even without feedback, repeated interaction partly restores commitment. Any equilibrium payoff from a partial-commitment persuasion model, where the sender may switch to policies preserving message marginals, shows up as a uniform payoff of the dynamic game. Convex mixes of such payoffs across message distributions also hold, and with state-independent payoffs the sender reaches the Bayesian persuasion payoff.
arxiv-2604-26743: Wang and nine colleagues analyze GAMA 376183, a powerful obscured nucleus in a low-mass galaxy likely merging. Found through strong neon emission, the source shows a column density over ten to the 23rd per square centimetre. Its X-ray luminosity nears ten to the 43rd erg per second. It ranks among few known obscured nuclei in low-mass galaxies. Its Eddington ratio of about four fifths signals rapid black-hole growth. Disturbed images and a starburst point to a merger driving accretion and starburst.
arxiv-2604-26843: Zambom and Wang introduce ARCH-m(X), a model for financial volatility in which outside factors act through an unknown smooth function. They build a test for whether factors matter, using an artificial one-way ANOVA design, and show its statistic tends to a standard normal law. They also build a variable-picking rule from Benjamini-Yekutieli false-discovery corrections to covariate p-values, which picks the true predictor set with probability tending to one. Simulations beat rivals, and an application to SP500 return volatility shows the method's practical use.
arxiv-2604-27143: Probst, Happe, and Cito study why small locally hosted open-weight language models fail at Linux privilege escalation, a penetration-testing subtask where cloud models raise privacy and sovereignty worries. Prior work puts small models at only 8 to 16 percent success on standard tasks. From execution traces they distill six recurring failure modes, map each to a known fix, and test five enhancements inside the hackingBuddyGPT framework under one shared harness.
arxiv-2604-27243: Liu, Song, Zhang, and Turner propose a chance-based framework linking preference uncertainty to decision uncertainty in engineering design. Design problems often combine several objectives into one utility score that picks an optimal design from the Pareto set. When preferences are imperfectly known, the chosen design is uncertain too. Treating preference parameters as random variables yields a distribution over optimal designs. That shows which Pareto regions are likeliest to win and how stable recommendations stay under preference shifts.
arxiv-2604-27343: Nguyen and six colleagues build JI-ADF, a three-way deep learning system for sorting skin lesions that combines dermoscopic images, clinical photographs, and patient records. Its design learns shared patterns across modalities while keeping signals unique to each source. It adjusts each modality's weight for every case through adaptive decision fusion plus a fusion attention step. Tested on the MILK10k benchmark, which mirrors messy real clinics with severe class imbalance, it improves sensitivity and Dice score while keeping specificity high and calibration sound.
arxiv-2604-27443: Guo and five colleagues present ABC, a method for making continuous-time, continuous-space random processes from partial views, such as first and last video frames. Older diffusion methods fail to capture how near-in-time states match, inject noise blind to time elapsed, and ignore any subsets of states. ABC models the process with a single ongoing stochastic differential equation whose clock and states track real time and process states. Tests show it beats rival methods on video generation and weather forecasting.
arxiv-2604-27543: Beck and six colleagues present AppTek Call-Center Dialogues, a benchmark of spontaneous, role-played agent-customer calls in English. The corpus covers fourteen English accents across sixteen service settings, with audio and text kept private until release to limit overlap with large pretraining data. They test several open-source speech recognition systems under varied segmentation methods. Scores varied widely by accent and method, showing that strong results on general American English tests do not always carry over to other accents.
arxiv-2604-27743: Domb shows that self-taught nets prefer normal curves, following the Information Bottleneck rule. Framing the Info Bottleneck goal as a rate-distortion problem gives a basis for optimal, target-neutral latent codes. They tend toward bell-shaped Gaussian states. Latent codes group inputs sharing forecast curves in a simplex structure. The framework joins taught and less-taught goals and explains smoothing. It derives usable loss goals matching this structure and offers a lens on collapse and codes.
arxiv-2604-27943: Zhang and colleagues demonstrate a quantum network that lets four users share secret keys over separate 11-kilometre links at the same time. Their continuous-variable design encodes keys in light waves and stays secure when judged on a finite batch of signals rather than an endless stream. The system adjusts protection and key speed for each user, fitting multi-user security onto ordinary telecom fibres.
arxiv-2604-28043: Ramachandran, Jha and Ramasubramanian present CARE, a step-by-step method for building science agents with experts, developers and helper agents. Helper agents turn loose domain aims into clear, checkable specs that humans sign off at stage gates, covering conduct, grounding, tools and checks. A science case study shows this staged way of working lifts build speed and hard-query results.
arxiv-2605-00143:
Yuxi Ma, Yongqian Peng, Junchen Lyu, Chi Zhang, and Yixin Zhu study why timing makes jokes land. Humor theory has long stressed semantic incongruity, the clash of meanings, while comedians insist timing is everything. The authors propose a Dual Prediction Violation framework to capture how content and timing interact as two kinds of broken expectation, and they test it on hundreds of pro Chinese stand-up performances.

Temporal features turn out to outweigh meaning clash in predicting audience enjoyment. Peak meaning violations matter more than average clash, and pauses lengthen in a set pattern before high-surprise punchlines, a planned coupling that separates successful from unsuccessful performances. The findings recast humor as temporally scaffolded: timing and content work in step, not on their own. The framework links humor research with predictive processing accounts of the brain.
arxiv-2605-00543:
Yusheng Niu, Hui Liu, and Zhihao Xu study a one-dimensional chain of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger type, a standard model of a topological insulator, with a quasiperiodic pattern in its hopping strengths. The pattern's shape is governed by an integer power and a tuning parameter that interpolates between a smooth profile and an abrupt sign-changing one. Their question is when topological phases reenter, vanishing and then returning as parameters move.

Combining a zero-mode localization criterion with a real-space topological indicator, they map phase diagrams in the limiting and intermediate regimes. A clean even-odd rule emerges. Odd powers give a zero-mean, sign-changing profile and can pull the system back into a topological phase from one trivial side. Even powers keep a positive mean and allow reentrance only from the opposite trivial side. The diagrams survive moderate hopping noise, suggesting a circuit realization.
arxiv-2605-00643:
Tim Harris reviews how to cut the statistical noise in lattice QCD, the grid-based form of the strong force used to compute particle traits from scratch. A large share of the cost of such forecasts lies in computing correlation functions on one set of gauge fields. The noise in those estimates hinges on the observable and on physical settings such as lattice spacing, volume, and gap, so knowing it is key to planning the runs.

The review, written as a conference write-up, covers quantities built from quark propagators, including both joined and split quark-line pieces. The schemes discussed split the propagators into pieces that can be worked on with different effort, putting the work where it pays. Such plans have already served exact physics well. Harris argues they may soon help reduce the cost of reaching the large volumes that frontier work demands.
arxiv-2605-00943:
Stavya Datta and three co-authors present ARIS, an agentic framework that gives social robots stronger relationship reasoning and longer conversations. Foundational models improved robot perception and communication, yet systems still struggle with multi-turn engagement and socially grounded dialogue. ARIS unifies multimodal reasoning, a graph-based Social World Model, and retrieval-based drafting in one modular design.

The Social World Model maps and updates links between users in a knowledge graph, supporting recognition across meetings. The retrieval pipeline keeps latency bounded even as histories grow to thousands of exchanges. Tested with a Pepper robot in dyadic conversation, ARIS scored much higher than a language-model baseline on perceived intelligence, animacy, human-likeness, and appeal in a small user study.
arxiv-2605-01543:
Shao Xian Lee and 23 co-authors clean structured artifacts out of X-ray images from high-energy-density experiments, where each shot may be the only one of its kind. Drifting patterns in the imaging system ride on top of the real signal. Standard flat-field correction leaves their ghosts in the final transmission maps, biasing measures of density, speed, and feature size.

The team model the artifacts as a separable layer and train a U-Net to estimate that layer from each shot. Against Fourier filtering and a dynamic flat-field method, the physics-guided network lifts image similarity scores from poor to near unity in synthetic tests, while keeping thin filament profiles intact. Deep ensembles add uncertainty estimates for each rebuild, a guard flagging shots unlike the training data. The method targets fusion and high-energy-density labs that cannot afford a spoiled single shot.
arxiv-2605-01843:
Jean-Baptiste Joinet and Carlos Olarte study binary relations through an agonistic lens, where one agent attacking another is the basic link. They look at properties defined on groups of four elements and ask when a derived notion of protection stays consistent. Their work connects that question to balance in signed networks, where allies agree inside a group and oppose those outside it.

The authors show that balance can be captured by one such four-element property, called collusivity. That gives a new way to test whether a network splits into opposed camps.
